description: A 10 m square and a 20 m square with a notch 10 m wide cut down from its top edge to z = 5,000. Every vertex of the inner square lies inside the outer polygon, two of them on the notch's sides, and no edge crosses an edge at a point interior to both: the edges only touch and share stretches. But the inner square's top edge runs across the notch, so the point (5,000, 8,000) lies inside the inner square and outside the outer polygon: the inner square does not lie inside it. A test of the vertices and of the crossings alone finds it inside; the midpoint of each piece of an inner edge between the points where it meets the outer boundary decides it (PRD v4 5.4.18 (10)).
name: notch-vertex
